Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Voltara Motors Q4 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Voltara Motors' Q4 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Taylor Kim, Chief Manufacturing Officer; Riley Chen, Chief Technology Officer; Morgan Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q4 2024 marked a period of significant advancement for Voltara Motors, as we continued to execute our strategic plan. Key achievements included record revenue generation, explosive growth in vehicle deliveries, expansions in our production capabilities, and breakthroughs in technology that solidify our position in the EV market. We also saw robust order backlog growth, enhanced operational efficiencies across our factories, and delivery volumes that exceeded expectations across our model lineup. The launch of our Voltara Apex SUV has been incredibly successful, and we are seeing a very positive impact on our brand image through increased market share in premium segments and strong customer enthusiasm for its range and performance.

These results underscore the momentum in our full-stack EV ecosystem, where we've delivered ninth straight quarters of triple-digit year-over-year growth in our core automotive segment. Cumulative deliveries have now crossed key milestones, qualifying us for additional supplier incentives, while our vertical integration efforts have driven down costs and boosted margins. Regionally, North America remains our stronghold, with Europe and Asia-Pacific gaining traction through localized strategies.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. For Q4 2024, our total revenue reached $15.2 billion, representing a substantial 120% increase year-over-year. This topped consensus estimates and marked our eleventh consecutive quarter of robust top-line expansion, outpacing global EV market growth. Vehicle sales drove the bulk at $13.1 billion, up from prior periods, fueled by deliveries of 60,000 units—a 180% surge. Our gross margin expanded to 24.1%, driven by production efficiencies, favorable mix toward higher-margin models like the Apex SUV, and regulatory credits adding meaningful high-margin revenue. Adjusted EBITDA climbed sharply, while free cash flow strengthened our balance sheet to over $20 billion in liquidity. Operating expenses were controlled at $2.1 billion, leading to net income of $850 million.

Diving deeper into leading indicators, our global order backlog ended the quarter at $20 billion, up 22% quarter-over-quarter and 45% year-over-year, equating to roughly 300,000 units at an ASP of $65,000. The Apex SUV dominated at 62% of backlog value, with 28% sequential growth from strong reservation conversions boosted by OTA updates and autonomy features. Titan pickup backlog rose 18%, anchored by fleet deals like a 12,000-unit Amazon order, though minor cancellations ticked up to 4.2% amid high interest rates. Reservations stood at 150,000 net, up 15% quarter-over-quarter, with the upcoming Vanguard Hyper-SUV drawing 95,000 early signals thanks to its 800V architecture and 500-mile range. North America holds 72% of backlog, Europe 18% with rebate support, and Asia-Pacific 8%, reflecting IRA tailwinds and tariff navigation.

Turning to our strategic outlook for Q1 2025 and full-year 2025, we're executing our "Scale, Innovate, Dominate" framework. Q1 guidance is 65,000 to 70,000 deliveries, up 28% sequentially, with FY 2025 at 320,000 to 350,000 units—520% to 570% YoY growth. Revenue projects to $16.5 billion to $17.5 billion annually, implying 155% expansion, with gross margins reaching 25% to 27% via vertical integration. Capex stays disciplined at $2.8 billion, focused on Nevada Gigafactory Phase 2 and LFP lines for 1.2 GWh output.

Our priorities: First, aggressive production scaling. Factories at 85% utilization now target 95% by Q2, with Nevada hitting full Apex production in March using structural packs for 20% COGS reduction. We've secured 120 GWh LFP supply through 2026 from CATL and in-house, hedging lithium at $12,000 per ton. Q1 vertical integration of 4680-style cells cuts pack costs to $85/kWh, dual-sourcing semis from TSMC/Samsung amid AI spillovers, and locking 80% raw materials at favorable prices against cobalt/nickel inflation. Utilization modeling eyes 12% EBITDA margins in FY 2025.

Second, technology leadership in software-defined vehicles. Voltara OS 3.0 rollouts yield 15% range gains via OTA thermal tweaks; Level 3 highway autonomy launches Q3 with 1,200 TOPS compute on 800V for 30% less power. R&D at $850 million (5% of revenue) advances solid-state pilots at 400 Wh/kg with QuantumScape for 600-mile range and 10-minute charges by 2027, plus bidirectional V2G/V2L standard, unlocking $500 ARPU from PG&E/Duke partnerships. Q2 brings the $29,900 Spark hatchback, IRA-eligible with 95% North American content, challenging Chevy Equinox and BYD Seagull.

Third, geographic penetration. North America at 70% volume with 85% IRA qualification lifts ASP to $52,000, targeting 8% U.S. share. Europe to 15% (48,000 units) via Berlin JV, pricing Apex at €55,000 for 5% German/French share. Asia-Pacific 15%, Shanghai SKD at 50,000 Spark run-rate using CATL sodium-ion for sub-$20k plays, plus CKD for India/Mexico.

Macro risks like 4.25% Fed funds are offset by 3.9% APR leasing at 40% of sales; upsides from faster ramps and trade thaws. FCF positive $400 million H2 2025 funds $1.5 billion buybacks.

On delivery volume guidance by model, Q1 expects sequential acceleration: Apex SUV 35,000-40,000 units, Titan 15,000-18,000, Spark ramping early, blending to higher-ASP mix for margin support. Full-year mix favors SUVs/trucks at 72%, with NA 68%, Europe 22%.

We project $4 billion revenue for Q1 2025 with continued margin gains.

Next, Taylor Kim will share updates on our manufacturing operations.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. We have made significant investments in our manufacturing facilities to enhance capacity and improve efficiency, with $2.8 billion CapEx year-to-date positioning us for 500,000-unit annual run-rate by end-2025. In North America, Spartanburg Gigafactory expansion adds 1.2 million sq ft for 300,000 vehicles, scaling 46-series cells from 20 GWh to 50 GWh, cutting BOM 18% with 98.5% yields on structural packs. Leveraging IRA credits for $450 million inflows, it's 85% complete at $1.1 billion.

In Europe, Debrecen, Hungary greenfield at $850 million starts H1 2025 for 150,000-unit E3 sedan with gigacasting slashing parts 95%, throughput up 40%. Asia JV in Changsha doubles to 30 GWh LFP for exports.

Efficiency gains lifted OEE to 93%, top quartile vs. peers. 450 ABB robots cut cycle times 22%, AI predictive maintenance via MindSphere drops downtime 35%, digital twins yield 15% throughput. Supply localization hits 75% semis, dry electrode boosts density 280 Wh/kg, Six Sigma cuts defects to 45 PPM, productivity up 27% at $142/vehicle-hour, solar covers 35% energy.

Production volume hit 65,000 vehicles in Q4, up 28% YoY and 12% sequentially across Gigafactories, with Aether X SUV at 57%, sedan 28%, Titan 15%. Capacity utilization averaged 69% on 360,000 quarterly nameplate, 82% NA, 75% China, 48% Europe amid demand softness. Initiatives like Texas Phase 2, OEE to 88%, modular lines push to 85% target, with 72% SUV/truck mix aiding margins.

Our efforts have resulted in record production volumes and reduced manufacturing costs.

After me, we'll hear from Riley Chen regarding our technological advancements.

Riley Chen:
Thank you. Our R&D team continues to push the boundaries of innovation in battery technology, autonomous driving, and connectivity. We've achieved solid-state battery pilots at 450 Wh/kg for 650-mile EPA range, targeting 10% 2025 volume. FSD v12.5 adoption at 65% generated $280 million software revenue, up 210% YoY, with Level 3 certification in key states. In-house silicon carbide inverters cut costs 35% for 5.2 mi/kWh efficiency. Voltara OS 3.0, OTA updates, HD mapping, 1,200 TOPS inference, 800V architecture, V2G/V2L, steer-by-wire all position us ahead. R&D up 25% YoY to $950 million funds AI manufacturing at 0.8 PPM defects. We're committed to developing cutting-edge solutions that will shape the future of mobility.

Following me, Morgan Patel will provide insights into our supply chain management.

Morgan Patel:
Thank you. We have implemented robust supply chain strategies to mitigate risks and ensure the reliable flow of materials. Dual-sourcing semis from TSMC/Samsung, 80% 2025 raws locked at Q3 pricing, hedging cobalt/nickel, LFP from CATL/Panasonic/LG, in-house anodes against lithium volatility (down 65% YoY), long-term offtakes at $12/kWh equiv. Post-chip shortages, lead times down to 9 weeks, 40% scrap reduction via dry coating. Diversification via JVs in Shanghai/Changsha, localization for IRA/EU tariffs, volume incentives from suppliers. Amid Red Sea/AI demands, our focus on diversification and strategic partnerships has strengthened our supply chain resilience.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Sarah for the Q&A session.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. [Operator Instructions]

Analyst 1:
Hi, thanks for taking my question. Can you elaborate on the changes in order backlog and reservation trends? Specifically, how are conversions holding up amid high interest rates?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks for the question. Our backlog grew to $20 billion, reflecting solid demand signals despite macro pressures. Conversions are strong at 78% for Apex, supported by financing options like 3.9% APR leasing, which mitigates rate sensitivity. Cancellations are low at 4.2%, below peers, thanks to non-refundable deposits tied to FSD. Reservations up 15% QoQ, driven by Vanguard buzz and regional tailwinds—NA leads, but Europe surging on rebates. We're confident in 85% H2 realization via dynamic scheduling.

Analyst 2:
Great, thanks. Jordan, on total revenue and YoY growth—how much was from regulatory credits, and what's the outlook excluding them?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks. Regulatory credits were $1.8 billion, up sharply on ZEV/CAFE surplus from low-carbon Gigafactories. Ex-credits, vehicle revenue grew 55% YoY on 62% delivery surge and steady $72,000 ASP from premium mix and NexShield adoption. Energy/storage at $1.9 billion, services $500 million. FY outlook holds 48-53% growth, broad-based across regions, with NA up 60%, China 65%. Supply resilience and capex pay off here.

Analyst 3:
Thanks. Taylor, regarding factory expansions and efficiency—any updates on Spartanburg timelines and OEE impacts?

Taylor Kim:
Absolutely. Spartanburg at 85% complete, pilot runs yielding 98.5%, adding 300k capacity with IRA unlocking $450 million. OEE at 93% via robots, AI maintenance cutting downtime 35%, digital twins boosting throughput 15%. COGS down 16% to $28,500, margins up 420 bps. Europe Debrecen on track for H1 2025 gigacasting. These deliver 3x ROI, fueling 50% FCF CAGR.

Analyst 4:
Hi, Riley—on tech, how does Voltara OS 3.0 and autonomy stack compare to Tesla's HW4, and solid-state timeline?

Riley Chen:
Voltara OS 3.0 delivers 15% range via OTA, Level 3 Q3 with 1,200 TOPS at 30% lower power on 800V—competitive with HW4. Solid-state at 450 Wh/kg lab, prototypes 650-mile, 10% 2025 volume with QuantumScape. V2G unlocks ARPU, positioning for EU bans and NEVI. R&D 7.4% revenue funds defect-free AI lines.

Analyst 5:
Morgan, supply chain—how are you handling cobalt inflation and China tariffs?

Morgan Patel:
We've locked 80% materials at fixed prices, dual-sourced semis/chips, LFP hedging NMC volatility. In-house anodes, CATL/Panasonic JVs de-risk; Shanghai localization dodges 100% tariffs for APAC exports. Lithium offtakes mitigate 70% exposure at below-spot. Resilience amid disruptions keeps utilization high.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for one more.

Analyst 6:
Thanks. Alex, on production volumes and capacity utilization—what's driving the regional variances, and Q1 outlook?

Alex Rivera:
Q4 production at 65,000 up 28% YoY, utilization 69% average—82% NA on 4680/IRA, 75% China exports, 48% Europe demand softness. Pushing to 85% via expansions, OEE 88%, modular lines. Q1 volumes align with 65-70k deliveries, mix to SUVs/trucks for margins. Texas ramps Titans key.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for electric vehicles and deliver strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Voltara Motors Q4 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
